To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the composition of milk is a consequence of co-evolutionary interactions between mothers and infants; and 2) the nutritional value of milk is the result of a co-evolutionary arms race between mothers and infants.
(1) mother's milk is a complete and balanced diet for the infant, and (2) milk composition reflects the co-evolution between milk producer and milk consumer.

mother's milk is a complex food that has been co-evolving in a symbiotic fashion with the infant for more than 200 million years, and that it provides the infant with all the nutrients required for optimal growth and development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the evolutionary context of food and its implications for the health of the consumer.
the evolutionary origins and consequences of human food and nutrition.
understanding the evolution and ecology of food and nutrition, and the implications for the future of human health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mother's milk is a perfect food for the infant and that it is an important reference food for all other food commodities.

the food we produce, process and eat today is a reflection of our evolutionary past and that the milk that a mother produces for her child is the Rosetta stone for the future of food and human nutrition.
mother's milk is the best food.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
'food is the mother's milk of evolution'.

the milk that a mammal produces for her young reflects the most sophisticated and complex diet ever produced by an animal, and that the capacity of the mother and her offspring to produce and use milk is an example of symbiotic coevolution.
the milk that a mother provides for her young reflects a complex interplay between the evolutionary pressures of the environment and the genetic endowment of the mother and infant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
milk is a'model food' and that the milk of other mammals provides a rich resource of biomolecules that may have applications in human health and food science.
mother's milk provides a blueprint for the design of optimal foods for human health and well-being.
the milk of all mammals is a complex and dynamic system of nutrients that is optimised to support the growth and development of young.
